explanation.headline: quickcache merges optional compression for cached values
explanation.whatHappened: The quickcache project merged a change that adds an optional compression setting for cached values.
explanation.previously: quickcache stored every value exactly as it was given, so large text values used a lot of memory.
explanation.whatChanged: A new compress option can shrink values before they are stored. It is off unless you turn it on.
explanation.whyItMatters: Apps that keep large text in quickcache could use less memory once this reaches a release. The change is merged into the main code but is not in a published version yet, so users do not have it.
explanation.nextConfirmed: No next step has been announced.
explanation.nextSpeculative: The option could appear in the project's next version.

glossary.definition: A fast, temporary store that keeps data close by so a program does not have to fetch it again.
Accepted into the project's main code. It still has to be included in a release before most people can use it.
Squeezing data so it takes up less space, then unpacking it when it is needed.

explanation.intermediate: Pull request #812 adds an opt-in compress flag. Values are compressed on write and decompressed on read.
explanation.technical: The change adds a compress option, off by default, intended to reduce memory for large text values. Behavior is unchanged unless the option is enabled.
